note: Offline learning-card content for the 20 FieldSnap classes. Written from the sources cited in docs/species_candidates.md; no images are bundled. Fields: slug (model label), common_name, scientific_name, group, maori_name, identification (short field marks), habitat (where a beginner will meet it), status (native/introduced/pest).

species.identification: Large dark honeyeater with an iridescent green-blue sheen, a white throat tuft and a distinctive curled black feather tuft on the neck. Two-note song with clicks and wheezes.
species.habitat: Native forest, bush remnants, and suburban gardens with flowering trees.

species.identification: Large heavy pigeon with a white chest and belly, dark green-purple iridescent back, and a loud whooshing wingbeat in flight.
species.habitat: Forest canopy and urban trees with fruit and leaves; often seen alone or in pairs.

species.identification: Small restless bird with a long fanned tail, white eyebrow, and a constant flitting, twisting flight as it hawks insects.
species.habitat: Bush edges, gardens, parks and stream sides; often follows people to catch disturbed insects.

species.identification: Tiny olive-green bird with a bold white eye-ring and a fine pointed bill; usually in fast-moving flocks.
species.habitat: Gardens, orchards and scrub; visits sugar-water feeders and small fruit.

species.identification: Olive-green honeyeater, slightly smaller and slimmer than a tūī, with a clear bell-like song and a reddish eye in the male.
species.habitat: Native bush and predator-free restoration areas; less common in dense suburbs than the tūī.

species.identification: Small stocky brown-grey bird; male has a grey crown and black bib, female is plain buff-brown with a pale stripe behind the eye.
species.habitat: Everywhere people are: streets, cafe tables, gardens, farm buildings.

species.identification: Adult male is all black with a yellow-orange bill and eye-ring; female is dark brown with a paler throat and faint mottling. Hops on lawns and flicks leaf litter.
species.habitat: Gardens, parks, forest floor and lawns, especially after rain.

species.identification: Warm brown above with a cream breast covered in clear dark speckles arranged in rows; smaller and more speckled than a female blackbird. Repeats each song phrase two or three times.
species.habitat: Gardens, parks and bush edges, often near snails, which it smashes on a favourite stone.

species.identification: Stubby, short-tailed bird; breeding adults are glossy black with iridescent green-purple sheen and pale speckles, with a yellow bill. Juveniles are dull grey-brown.
species.habitat: Open lawns, car parks, playing fields and city buildings; flocks and murmurations.

species.identification: Chunky chocolate-brown bird with a black hood, bare yellow skin around the eye, and white wing patches that flash in flight. Loud, varied calls; walks rather than hops.
species.habitat: Urban lawns, roadsides and shopping-centre car parks; strongly associated with people.

species.identification: Coastal tree with dense leathery dark-green leaves that are white and felted underneath, and masses of crimson brush-like flowers from November to January. Aerial roots hang from older trunks.
species.habitat: Coastal cliffs and seaside reserves; widely planted as a street and garden tree in Auckland.

species.identification: Tall tree with a stout trunk and one or more branches, each ending in a dense tuft of long narrow sword-shaped leaves. Large panicles of small creamy flowers in spring.
species.habitat: Swamps, damp flats and open ground; extremely common in Auckland streets, parks and gardens.

species.identification: Clump of long stiff upright blade-like leaves, often 2 m tall, with a red-orange midrib and flower and a tall dull-red flower spike. Leaves do not have a distinct keel like the mountain flax.
species.habitat: Wetland margins, coastal flats and gardens; very common in Auckland plantings.

species.scientific_name: Alsophila dealbata (syn. Cyathea dealbata, Alsophila tricolor)
species.identification: Tree fern with a slender trunk and a crown of fronds whose undersides are strikingly white, visible when fronds turn over. Dead fronds form a skirt on the trunk.
species.habitat: Damp forest and bush remnants; also planted in gardens and reserves.

species.identification: The only mainland New Zealand palm: a straight ringed trunk topped by a crown of long fronds that all rise from a smooth green bulbous base. Red berry-like fruit in clusters.
species.habitat: Lowland and coastal forest, especially in the northern North Island; common in Auckland bush remnants.

species.identification: Small tree with tiny paired oval leaflets and hanging clusters of bright yellow flowers in early spring. Seed pods are long, dry and constricted between the seeds.
species.habitat: Stream banks, forest margins and gardens; widely planted and much visited by tūī and korimako.

species.identification: Low creeping ground cover with glossy dark-green pointed leaves about 5 cm long, forming dense mats. Small three-petalled white flowers in summer. Stems root at every node.
species.habitat: Shaded forest floor, stream banks and gardens; a serious smothering weed in Auckland bush.

species.identification: Shrub or small tree with large soft grey-green felted leaves and clusters of small purple flowers with yellow centres, followed by dull yellow round berries. All parts have a strong smell when crushed.
species.habitat: Disturbed ground, roadsides, forest margins and waste areas; a declared Auckland pest plant.

species.identification: Bold ginger with large glossy leaves arranged in two ranks on thick stems up to 2 m tall, topped by a spike of pale yellow flowers with prominent red stamens. Spreads by thick branching rhizomes.
species.habitat: Shaded forest floor and stream sides where it forms dense stands; a major Auckland pest plant.

species.identification: Vigorous twining vine with dark green opposite leaves and small cream-white bell flowers; distinctive large grey-green choko-like pods that split to release silky seeds. Milky white sap.
species.habitat: Forest margins, fences, hedges and waste ground; smothers shrubs. A declared Auckland pest plant.
